title: 〜や否や / 〜や
simpleExplanation: 〜や否や (or just 〜や) means "the moment X happened, Y happened": ドアが開くや否や、客がなだれ込んだ. The dictionary form comes before it, even though the event is in the past. Y is something that actually happened, usually sudden and vivid, never a command or plan.
whenUsed: Formal written Japanese: news, novels, reports. In speech, とたん(に) or 〜てすぐ are used. The shorter 〜や is even more literary. Both stress that there was no gap at all between X and Y.
formation: Y = an actual past event, often sudden (飛び出した・なだれ込んだ・売り切れた)

rows.label: 〜が早いか
cells: Y is a quick deliberate action

examples.ja: ドアが開くや否や、客が店内になだれ込んだ。
examples.reading: ドアがひらくやいなや、きゃくがてんないになだれこんだ。
examples.en: The moment the doors opened, customers surged into the store.
examples.note: Dictionary form 開く + や否や; Y is a vivid past event.

examples.ja: 彼はベルが鳴るや、教室を飛び出した。
examples.reading: かれはベルがなるや、きょうしつをとびだした。
examples.en: As soon as the bell rang, he dashed out of the classroom.
examples.note: Short form 〜や with the same meaning.

examples.ja: 新製品は発売されるや否や、売り切れになった。
examples.reading: しんせいひんははつばいされるやいなや、うりきれになった。
examples.en: The new product sold out as soon as it was released.
examples.note: Passive dictionary form 発売される + や否や.

examples.ja: 彼は駅に着くや否や、会社に電話をかけた。
examples.reading: かれはえきにつくやいなや、かいしゃにでんわをかけた。
examples.en: The moment he reached the station, he phoned the office.
examples.note: Same subject in both clauses is common.

examples.ja: その噂が流れるや、株価は急落した。
examples.reading: そのうわさがながれるや、かぶかはきゅうらくした。
examples.en: As soon as the rumour spread, the share price plunged.

similarGrammar.difference: Same timing, but Y is a quick, deliberate action by the subject (飛び出した). や否や can also describe reactions and events.
Same subject required; Y is unexpected. Also written.
"No sooner than (repeatedly)": describes a habit that keeps recurring, not a single event.

commonMistakes.wrong: ドアが開いたや否や、客が入った。
commonMistakes.right: ドアが開くや否や、客が入った。
commonMistakes.why: The dictionary form is required before や否や, even for past events.

commonMistakes.wrong: 家に帰るや否や、手を洗いなさい。
commonMistakes.right: 家に帰ったらすぐ、手を洗いなさい。
commonMistakes.why: Y cannot be a command; や否や reports what actually happened.

commonMistakes.wrong: ベルが鳴るや否や、彼は教室を出るつもりだ。
commonMistakes.right: ベルが鳴るや否や、彼は教室を飛び出した。
commonMistakes.why: Y is a completed event, not an intention.

usageNotes: Y is usually dramatic: crowds rushing, prices crashing, someone dashing out.
や否や literally means "whether or not": "barely had X happened (or not) when Y".
News writers like the shorter 〜や for headlines and lead sentences.
jlptTips: A dictionary-form verb before the blank and a sudden past event after it → や否や.
Distractors: が早いか, なり, とたん. Check the form: とたん takes Vた; the others take Vる. Between や否や and が早いか, the exam usually accepts either only when the meaning differs.
Eliminate any option if the second clause is a command, request or intention.
